print_area._note: REAL print area, from Evan reading the Tapstitch editor 14 Sep 2026, replacing the placeholder canvas. editor_px is what the editor states and editor_dpi is the resolution those pixels are quoted at. 150 CONFIRMED (see below); it was also the only reading under which the design fits at all (at 300 the widest back area is 6.9in across and a 12in temple is impossible). It also lands within half an inch of the 14.98in Printify area this catalogue printed on for a year. width_px and height_px are the editor numbers doubled, so the exported PNG is 300dpi at final size rather than 150; the aspect ratio is identical to the pixel, so 'upload, centre, full size' places it the same way. If the editor turns out to quote 300dpi, change editor_dpi and every inch in the layout halves: nothing else needs touching. CONFIRMED 16 Sep 2026 from Tapstitch's own API rather than a reading of the editor: the crew template's backSideDpiTip reads "Print area size 2061 x 2757 px (150)DPI", which is exactly editor_px and editor_dpi below. The 150 is no longer an assumption.

front_print_area._ink_note: Both numbers are measured on the logo's ink, not its file frame. The logo PNG carries about 2.4% transparent padding across and 6.4% down, so the old frame-width rule printed a 5.86in logo where the config said 6.0in.

_naming_note: Was 'Classic Temple Crew Sweatshirt', then 'Cloud Temple Crew Sweatshirt' from 16 Sep 2026. EVAN, 17 Sep 2026: renamed again to 'Ultra-soft Temple Sweatshirt' (dropping 'Crew' from the name) to lead with feel instead of a cut name, matching the hoodie's new 'Ultra-soft Oversized Temple Hoodie' naming. This config only governs titles for every sweatshirt generated from here on; existing live products keep whatever title they were published with until changed by hand. The rest of the 16 Sep reasoning still applies: this closes the 'whether the product line names carry over' question in BRAND.md section 7, and renaming costs nothing extra because a replacement never inherited its predecessor's web address by title anyway -- Shopify builds the address from the title, so the address is always set explicitly with productUpdate(handle:) after publish. The retiring Printify configs (cc1566, cc1567) keep their old titles, because the live products they describe still carry them.

fulfillment._note: Evan, 14 Sep 2026: every line moves to USA fulfillment. Production 1-2 days and shipping 3-5 days, so 4-7 days to a customer's door against 10-17 from the international center. shipping_method is null because the US center's own service name was not read off the product page; the international options (Special Line, Special Line Pro, International Express) do not apply. Confirm the service name and the technique in the first editor session.
fulfillment._technique_note: DTF, not the DTG the UT0044 used. DTF lays a film layer on the fabric and gives strong opacity on dark grounds, which suits white line art, but large solid areas breathe less.

costs_usd._all_in_note: EVAN'S FIGURE, 14 Sep 2026, and the one to trust. Includes the blank, printing both sides, shipping, custom neck tag, hangtag, order insert, and payment gateway fees. Revised for USA fulfillment. The per-shipment line items that used to sit here were international rates and are gone rather than left to mislead; nothing below sums to all_in_per_unit.
costs_usd._blank_note: Read off the live product page 14 Sep 2026. Priced the same from the US and international centers.

_colorways_note: tapstitch is the name in their editor; shopify is what the storefront shows, renamed after publish. ink is which art file that colorway prints. Two colourways only: the US fulfillment center carries a narrower range than the international one, which is the trade for the faster shipping. NAMES VERIFIED 16 Sep 2026 against the store-product prefill, which is what Tapstitch sends Shopify: it says 'Black' and 'Flower Gray', so the rename and the colour reorder will both find what they are told to look for. INK DECIDED 16 Sep 2026: WHITE, on Evan's call after seeing the mockup. The question was real, not theoretical: Flower Gray is RGB(184,181,186), a mid heather, and white line art on it reads noticeably weaker than on black. He kept white knowingly, because a black-ink version of one colourway would be a SEPARATE PRODUCT: a Tapstitch template binds one design to a LIST of colour codes, so there is no per-colourway design the way Printify has colourway groups. Checked, not assumed: all ten variants of the crew's store-product prefill carry the same templateId and commitId. A THIRD US colourway exists and is deliberately excluded: 6672 Oat Gray, RGB(237,233,221), which is light and would print the black art.
_preview_color_note: Review-sheet background only, a provisional mid-gray standing in for Flower Gray, the colour this line now opens on. Replace it once the real swatch is on screen. Not a colour spec and nothing prints from it.
_spacing_note: Evan, 14 Sep 2026, superseding the earlier spacing: the temple and the location line are simply centred in the print file, vertically and horizontally, with the temple ink spanning no more than 12.0in at its widest point, the location line 0.7in of INK tall (not box), and the top of that line 0.5in below the temple's lowest ink. There is no top or bottom margin requirement any more, which is why both are 0.0 here: they were measured off the Printify back-stack layout, where the logo sat at the bottom of the back, and centring made them meaningless. They were also the only thing stopping tall temples reaching full width. The retiring Printify profiles keep 0.6 and 2.5 in spacing_defaults.json, untouched.
